Sanjeev AI: Architecture, Storage & Billing Specifications (v1.3) ​

This document defines the structural requirements for Sanjeev AI, a multi-user, project-based SaaS platform. Version 1.3 updates the architecture to reflect reality by moving character and location maps to the project level, chunking scripts into timelines, and tracking workflow execution states.

1. Authentication & User Management ​

We will implement Firebase Authentication with Google Sign-In as the primary identity provider.

  • Provider: Google (providerId: google.com).
  • Behavior:
    • Sign Up / Login: Handled automatically by the Firebase Auth UI.
    • User Creation Trigger: On the first sign-in, a users/{userId} document must be created in Firestore if it doesn't exist.
    • Session: Persisted via Firebase SDK default behavior (IndexedDB/LocalStorage).

2. Firestore Data Model (The Hierarchy) ​

We are moving from a root-level scripts collection to a hierarchical, user-centric model.

2.1 Data Storage Principle: Native Maps vs. Stringified JSON (NEW) ​

To handle complex configuration data like workflows, character maps, and vibe maps, this architecture mandates the use of native Firestore data types (Maps and Arrays) over stringified JSON.

  • Anti-Pattern (Forbidden): Storing settings as a single string.
    json
    // (DO NOT DO THIS) 
{ "workflowSteps": "[{\"stepId\":\"...\"}]" }
  • Required Pattern (Native Maps/Arrays): Storing settings as native, nested objects.
    json
    // (CORRECT) 
{ "workflowSteps": [ { "stepId": "..." } ] }

Justification:

  • Queryability: Native maps allow for direct, dot-notation queries (e.g., where("steps.action", "==", "PUBLISH_YOUTUBE")). Stringified JSON is un-queryable.
  • Atomic Updates: Native maps allow for updating a single, nested field (e.g., docRef.update({"characterMap.NARRATOR.voiceName": "new-voice"})). This is fast, cheap, and avoids race conditions. Stringified JSON requires a slow and unsafe "read-modify-write" of the entire blob.
  • Scalability: Native maps are handled efficiently by Firestore. Stringified JSON blobs can unexpectedly hit the 1 MiB document size limit and are unmanageable.

2.2 Root Collection: users ​

Path: users/{userId}

Document Fields:

  • uid: string (The User ID, matching the Document ID)
  • email: string
  • displayName: string
  • createdAt: timestamp
  • lastLogin: timestamp
  • plan: "free" | "pro" (for future billing logic)
  • credits: number (Balance for premium features like Cloud Rendering)
  • youtubeAccessToken: string (Optional. For YouTube publishing integration)
  • youtubeTokenTimestamp: number (Optional. Tracks token age for expiration)

2.3 Sub-Collection: projects (The Workspace) ​

Path: users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}

Document Fields:

  • name: string (e.g., "My Audio Book")
  • createdAt: timestamp
  • voiceEngine: "standard" | "gemini" (Default setting, can be overridden by Voice Lab)
  • stats: { scriptCount: number, audioCount: number }
  • defaultWorkflowId: string (Nullable. The ID of the workflow to run by default)
  • characterMap: object (A native Map defining character appearances and voice models. Shared across all scripts. See Principle 2.1)
  • locationMap: object (A native Map defining environment settings. See Principle 2.1)

2.4 Sub-Collection: workflows (The Orchestrator) ​

Path: users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/workflows/{workflowId}

Description: Defines a multi-step, customizable sequence of actions.

Storage: This MUST be stored as a native Firestore Map containing an Array of Map objects (see Principle 2.1).

Document Fields:

  • name: string (e.g., "Multilingual (EN+TA) Video")
  • type: "predefined" | "custom"
  • createdAt: timestamp
  • steps: array (An ordered list of Step Objects)

2.5 Workflow Step Object (Definition) ​

A Step Object is a Map (object) within the steps array.

Fields:

  • stepId: string (A unique ID for this step, e.g., "step_01_gen_audio_en")
  • name: string (A user-facing name, e.g., "Generate English Audio")
  • action: string (An enum defining the task, e.g., "GENERATE_AUDIO", "GENERATE_OVERVIEW", "PUBLISH_YOUTUBE")
  • dependsOn: array of strings (Lists stepIds that must complete first, e.g., ["step_01_gen_audio_en"])
  • config: object (Map of settings specific to this action)

2.6 Sub-Collection: scripts (The Core Asset) ​

Path: users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/scripts/{scriptId}

Description: Stores the text, timeline chunks, and creative settings for a single audio/video artifact.

Document Fields:

  • status: "uploaded" | "generating" | "complete"
  • content: string (Raw script body — stored as content in Firestore, sent as script to AI agents)
  • timeline: array (Array of line objects mapping scenes, speakers, and text)
  • vibeMap: object (A native Map. See Principle 2.1)
  • previewLibrary: object (A native Map. See Principle 2.1)
  • workflowState: object (A native Map tracking the real-time execution state of the active workflow)
  • finalAudioUrl: string
  • finalVideoUrl: string (Optional. Stored when video export finishes)
  • youtubeVideoUrl: string (Optional. Populated when successfully published to YouTube)
  • publishProgress: number (Optional. Used by Unified Studio for progress tracking)
  • publishStatus: string (Optional. Used by Unified Studio for status messages)

2.7 Sub-Collection: video_drafts (The Visual Project) ​

Path: users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/video_drafts/{draftId}

Description: Stores visual scenes, image prompts, and media URLs for video generation.

Document Fields:

  • projectId: string
  • scriptId: string (References the parent script)
  • title: string
  • status: string (e.g., "analyzed", "generating", "complete")
  • createdAt: timestamp
  • characterMapSnapshot: object (Frozen state of character appearances used for this specific generation)
  • scenes: array (List of generated visual scene objects, image/video URLs, prompts, and status)

2.8 Sub-Collection: notifications (User Inbox) ​

Path: users/{userId}/notifications/{notificationId}

Description: Stores background alerts and asynchronous completion updates.

Document Fields:

  • title: string
  • message: string
  • type: "success" | "error" | "info"
  • read: boolean (Default: false)
  • actionUrl: string (Deep link to related project/video)
  • createdAt: timestamp

2.8 Sub-Collection: usage (Billing Metrics) ​

Path: users/{userId}/usage/{monthDocId}

Doc ID Format: YYYY-MM (e.g., 2025-11)

Document Fields: (Counters updated via FieldValue.increment)

  • estimated_cost_usd: number (Total monthly spend)
  • cost_by_service: object (e.g., { cloud_tts: 0.12, imagen: 0.04 })
  • cost_by_project: object (e.g., { proj_123: 0.45 })
  • tts_standard_chars: number
  • tts_wavenet_chars: number
  • tts_neural2_chars: number
  • tts_studio_chars: number
  • tts_journey_chars: number
  • gemini_input_tokens: number
  • gemini_output_tokens: number
  • video_seconds: number (Veo video duration)
  • image_call: number (Imagen call count)
  • bytes: number (Total storage bytes added)

2.10 Sub-Collection: billing_ledger (Audit Trail) ​

Path: users/{userId}/billing_ledger/{eventId}

Document Fields: (Immutable ledger entries)

  • timestamp: serverTimestamp
  • projectId: string
  • scriptId: string | null
  • agentName: string (e.g., "parser", "generator", "cloud_renderer")
  • service: string (e.g., "cloud_tts", "vertex_ai_gemini", "cloud_run")
  • metric: string (e.g., "studio_chars", "input_tokens", "cloud_render_minutes")
  • quantity: number
  • unit_cost_usd: number
  • total_cost_usd: number (quantity * unit_cost_usd)

3. Cloud Storage Hierarchy ​

text
gs://{bucketName}/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/...
  ├── /raw/                .../{scriptId}_original.pdf
  ├── /processing/{scriptId}/ .../chunk_001.mp3
  ├── /audio/              .../{scriptId}_final.mp3
  ├── /previews/           .../{characterName}_{voiceName}_{style}.mp3
  ├── /workflow_outputs/   .../{workflowId}/{stepId}.mp4
  ├── /visuals/            .../{draftId}/scene_{index}_{timestamp}.{ext}
  └── /renders/            .../final_render_{timestamp}.webm

4. Billing Metrics & Observability Strategy ​

4.1 Billing Metrics ​

(No changes from v1.1)

  • Metric 1: TTS Usage (agent3_generator, agent3_preview)
  • Metric 2: GenAI Usage (agent1_parser, notebook_llm)
  • Metric 3: Storage Usage (aggregator, agent3_preview)

4.2 Client-Side Error Logging ​

To support "Support Readiness", the architecture requires a structured client-side error capture mechanism:

  • Integration: Errors caught in the React frontend (e.g., via React Error Boundaries or unhandled promise rejections) will be transmitted securely to Google Cloud Logging.
  • Payload Structure: Each log entry must include contextual metadata (userId, projectId, scriptId), the raw error message, stack trace, and the browser's user agent.
  • Endpoint: This will be handled either via a dedicated Cloud Function acting as a logging proxy, or direct Firebase integration.
